title: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values
abstract: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.
